compatibility.note: This is an expanded v2 knowledge schema. Update the advisory loader to read conditions_by_id/conditions and the renamed fields; it is not guaranteed to be a drop-in replacement for an unknown existing JSON schema.

safety.dose_policy: No pesticide doses are stored in this KB. Doses depend on formulation and change with label revisions. The advisory must always say: follow the current product label.
safety.chemical_policy: Chemical candidates in this file are unverified knowledge-base hints, not prescriptions. Before showing any active ingredient, the backend must verify current CIB&RC registration for the exact crop, pest/disease, formulation and use; if verification is unavailable, show non-chemical steps and refer to KVK. Never generate a dose. Follow the current product label for dose, PPE, re-entry interval and PHI.
never_recommend: any pesticide not registered with CIB&RC for the crop
safety.never_recommend_note: Banned or restricted in India for many crops. The backend TF-IDF safety retriever remains the authority: keep it in sync with the CIB&RC list.
safety.universal_safety_note: Follow the current product label for dose, protective equipment, re-entry period and pre-harvest interval. Never mix pesticides unless the label allows it. Keep sprays away from water sources and bees. Use only products registered for this crop. Check with the KVK or agriculture officer before you spray.
safety.disclaimer: This is decision support from an AI system and ICAR-based guidance. It does not replace a local agriculture officer, KVK or plant protection expert.

chemical_candidate_gate.if_verification_unavailable: Do not name a chemical; provide non-chemical actions and refer to KVK/agriculture officer.

safety.weather_missing_behavior: State that field weather is unavailable; do not assume conditions from regional defaults.

confidence_policy.note: Matches the pipeline: disease confidence below 0.70 goes to expert review. Below that, use the low_confidence fallback and still add weather and scouting guidance, but no chemical advice.

definition.Low: under 15 percent of the scanned leaf area

severity_model.caveat: Severity is measured on the scanned leaf by an HSV colour heuristic. It is not field incidence. The advisory engine must treat field spread as a separate input (field_incidence_pct) from scouting or repeat scans, and must say so when it is unknown.

field_area_policy.treat_whole_field_rule_of_thumb: If the disease or pest appears at about 1 in 5 or more sampling points, or the weather is blight-favourable, treat the whole field; use the local KVK threshold if it is known.
field_area_policy.spray_planning: Compute tanks as ceil(area_acre x litres_per_acre_from_label / tank_litres). Never invent litres per acre: read it from the product label or the sprayer calibration.

Cotton.gujarat_season: Kharif: sown Jun to Jul, picking Oct to Jan. Irrigated early sowings possible from May.
Cotton.host_notes: Okra and hibiscus (Malvaceae) are alternate hosts for whitefly-borne leaf curl; avoid planting them next to cotton.

avoid: cotton after cotton in the same plot
rotation.min_break_note: Break wilt-affected plots with non-hosts for 3 or more seasons.

Cotton.sensitive: Squaring to boll development: leaf diseases and sucking pests cause most yield loss.

Groundnut.gujarat_season: Kharif: sown Jun to Jul (Saurashtra main belt), harvest Oct to Nov. Summer crop: sown Jan to Feb, harvest May.
Groundnut.host_notes: Leaf spots and rust carry over on volunteer groundnut and crop debris.

avoid: other legumes with shared leaf spot hosts in the same season
rotation.min_break_note: Rotate with a cereal at least every second season.

Groundnut.sensitive: Flowering to pod development: leaf spot and rust defoliation reduces pod fill and fodder quality.

Pepper Bell.gujarat_season: Mainly Rabi (transplant Sep to Nov) and protected cultivation; also kharif in some areas.
Pepper Bell.host_notes: Shares pests and diseases with tomato, potato, brinjal, chilli and tobacco (Solanaceae).

rotation.min_break_note: Break 2 to 3 seasons from Solanaceae after bacterial or soil-borne disease.

Pepper Bell.sensitive: Flowering and early fruit set: stress and humidity cause flower drop, fruit disorders and fruit disease.

Potato.gujarat_season: Rabi: planted Oct to Nov (north Gujarat, Deesa belt), harvested Feb to Mar.
Potato.host_notes: Late blight and bacterial wilt also infect tomato and brinjal; volunteers and cull piles carry blight.

avoid: potato after potato in the same plot
rotation.min_break_note: Break 3 or more seasons from Solanaceae in bacterial wilt or nematode plots.

Potato.sensitive: Tuber initiation to bulking: foliage loss in these stages cuts tuber yield sharply.

Tomato.gujarat_season: Year-round in pockets: kharif (transplant Jun to Jul), rabi (Sep to Nov), summer (Jan to Feb).
Tomato.host_notes: Shares pests and diseases with potato, pepper, brinjal, chilli and tobacco (Solanaceae).

rotation.min_break_note: Break 2 to 3 seasons from Solanaceae after bacterial wilt, nematodes or virus.

Tomato.sensitive: Flowering to fruiting: leaf loss exposes fruit and raises sunscald; virus before 40 days after transplanting causes the biggest loss.

optional.field_area_ha: Numeric field area in hectares; convert units explicitly and flag locally variable vigha values

optional.sowing_or_transplant_date: ISO date; compute approximate crop stage from crop metadata
optional.last_sprays: List of {active, resistance_group, date, crop, target}
optional.scan_history_for_this_plot: Prior scans with timestamp, diagnosis, confidence and severity
optional.soil_test: pH, nutrients, texture and test date if known

missing_data_rules: Do not invent weather, field size, crop history, spray history, soil results or days to harvest.
Say when a factor is unknown.
If no field GPS/weather is available, provide only crop, diagnosis and stage guidance that does not depend on current weather.

diagnosis_confidence.action: Use low_confidence fallback; no chemical advice; request clearer photos and expert review.
Use expert fallback; do not infer a disease or pesticide.

definition.Low: under 15 percent of the scanned leaf area

severity.important_distinction: Image-level leaf severity is not field incidence. Use field_incidence_pct only when provided from scouting.

humid_warm_blight.note: Matches the backend blight risk rule.

cool_humid.note: Late blight and leaf mold weather.

warm_humid.note: Bacterial and fungal leaf disease weather.

hot_dry.note: Mites, thrips, whitefly and powdery mildew weather.

heat_stress.note: Matches the backend heat stress rule (38 C or more).

heavy_rain.note: Matches the backend flood rule (20 mm or more in 24 h).

moderate_rain.note: Rain splash that spreads leaf spots.

rain_expected_6h.note: Do not spray; product washes off.

prolonged_leaf_wetness.note: Use measured leaf wetness if present, else RH at or above 90 percent for 6 or more hours.

drought_stress.note: Wilt symptoms show faster; irrigate steadily.

cold_snap.note: Phosphorus purpling, slow growth, edema on warm days after cold nights.

spray_window_bad.note: Also true if temperature is 35 C or more or rain is forecast within 6 hours. Do not spray.

weather.spray_gate: If rain is forecast within 6 hours, wind is at least 15 km/h, or temperature is at least 35 C, suppress chemical-spray advice and explain the relevant weather constraint. This is a conservative advisory gate; the product label and local extension guidance remain authoritative.
weather.signal_precedence: Observed measurements first, then forecast values; never infer missing values.

rules.if: previous crop is in the same family as the current crop
rules.effect: raise soil-borne and carry-over disease risk; recommend rotation next season

rules.if: same crop grew in the plot in the last season
rules.effect: raise soil-borne and residue-borne risk; ask about debris removal

rules.if: the same diagnosis appeared in the last 2 seasons or in an earlier scan of this plot
rules.effect: escalate earlier and recommend resistant variety, seed treatment and rotation

rules.if: severity rank rose compared with the previous scan within 14 days
rules.effect: raise urgency one level and say it is getting worse

rules.if: last spray used the same resistance group as a candidate chemical
rules.effect: drop that candidate and prefer another group; never advise two consecutive sprays of one group

rules.if: 3 or more sprays of fungicide or insecticide already this season
rules.effect: emphasise non-chemical steps, resistance management and expert contact

rules.if: a spray was applied within the last 5 days
rules.effect: advise waiting and re-scouting unless the disease is blight-class

crop_stage.late_stage_note: Close to harvest: check the label pre-harvest interval first, prefer non-chemical steps, harvest healthy produce first, and keep affected produce separate.
crop_stage.stage_source: If sowing or transplant date is known, compute days after sowing (DAS) or transplanting (DAT) and map to the crop stage ranges (approximate; varieties differ). A farmer-entered stage overrides the computed one.

medium.management: W-pattern scouting, patch or whole-field decision

large.management: split into blocks of up to 1 ha

field_area.treat_whole_field_rule_of_thumb: If the disease or pest appears at about 1 in 5 or more sampling points, or the weather is blight-favourable, treat the whole field; use the local KVK threshold if it is known.
field_area.spray_planning: Compute tanks as ceil(area_acre x litres_per_acre_from_label / tank_litres). Never invent litres per acre: read it from the product label or the sprayer calibration.
field_area.large_field_note: On fields above 2 ha, plan sprays in 1 to 2 days with a weather gate and keep a block log. Prioritise the infected, upwind and low-lying blocks.

expert_escalation.when_escalated: Make expert escalation explicit in the first sentence of immediate_action; provide safe non-chemical steps only unless verified local guidance is available.

output_contract.language: Write in simple English at about grade 6 level. The pipeline translates to Hindi and Gujarati afterwards; keep sentences short and avoid idioms.
rules: Use only facts and options from the provided KB entry and context. Do not add products, doses, or claims that are not in them.
Never write a pesticide dose. Say to follow the label.
Start with non-chemical steps. Mention a chemical class only when the severity playbook says chemical_stance allows it.
If weather says do not spray, say so first.
If escalate_to_expert is true, say it clearly in the first sentence of immediate_action.
Say what in the weather, history, area or stage changed the advice, in why_this_advice.
Do not state that a diagnosis is confirmed solely from an image classifier.
Do not expose unverified chemical candidates to the farmer.
Use only provided context; distinguish measured facts from conditional risk.
When a condition is not in the KB, use fallback rather than nearest-match guessing.
